en.bio_html: My research centers on spatiotemporal traffic modeling and traffic safety and driving behavior. I combine statistical modeling, complex networks and physics-informed learning to study traffic-state reconstruction, crash risk and car-following dynamics. I am a Ph.D. student at Tsinghua University, advised by Prof. Ruimin Li. I previously completed my master’s studies at Central South University under the supervision of Prof. Jaeyoung Jay Lee.

publications.title: Do traffic flow states follow Markov properties? A high-order spatiotemporal traffic state reconstruction approach for traffic prediction and imputation
publications.authors: Hu, J., Hu, C., Yang, J., Bai, J., & Lee, J. J.
publications.contribution_html: Combines delayed state reconstruction with high-order spatial neighborhoods to represent traffic flow. Markov-property tests support a prior-informed autoencoder for missing-data imputation on PeMS datasets.
publications.caption: Research figure supplied with the original website. Do traffic flow states follow Markov properties? A high-order spatiotemporal traffic state reconstruction approach for traffic prediction and imputation

publications.title: A Simple Yet Efficient K-Nearest Neighbor-Based Method for High-Resolution Traffic Time–Space Diagram Imputation
publications.authors: Hu, J., Lee, J. J., Bai, J., & Mao, S.
publications.journal: Transportation Research Record: Journal of the Transportation Research Board
publications.contribution_html: Reconstructs high-resolution traffic time–space diagrams using adaptive, iterative K-nearest-neighbor imputation. Error-propagation analysis and experiments on Ubiquitous Traffic Eyes, NGSIM and highD examine the accuracy–efficiency trade-off.
publications.caption: Research figure supplied with the original website. A Simple Yet Efficient K-Nearest Neighbor-Based Method for High-Resolution Traffic Time–Space Diagram Imputation

publications.title: Crash risk prediction using sparse collision data: Granger causal inference and graph convolutional network approaches
publications.authors: Hu, J., Bai, J., Yang, J., & Lee, J. J.
publications.contribution_html: PST-CGCN combines historical spatiotemporal data enhancement with a Granger-based association graph for crash-risk prediction. Evaluation on New York City data examines short-term risk identification and spatial relationships.
publications.caption: Research figure supplied with the original website. Crash risk prediction using sparse collision data: Granger causal inference and graph convolutional network approaches

publications.title: Dynamic correlation analysis of urban crashes using Tucker-net based SIRS model: A case study in New York City
publications.authors: Hu, J., Bai, J., Zhang, J., Byon, Y.-J., & Lee, J. J.
publications.contribution_html: Integrates Tucker decomposition with a modified SIRS model to describe dynamic relationships among urban crash zones. New York City experiments examine temporal patterns, predictive performance and parameter stability.
publications.caption: Research figure supplied with the original website. Dynamic correlation analysis of urban crashes using Tucker-net based SIRS model: A case study in New York City

publications.title: Dynamic Safety Estimation of Airport Pick-Up Area Based on Video Trajectory Data
publications.authors: Yang, J., Lee, J., Mao, S., & Hu, J.
publications.journal: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems
publications.contribution_html: Estimates dynamic safety in airport pick-up areas from video-derived vehicle trajectories. Surrogate conflict indicators and Modified CUSBoost classification connect maneuver patterns with conflict risk.
publications.caption: Research schematic prepared from the published abstract; not an original figure.

publications.title: Analysis of injury severity of single-vehicle and two-vehicle crashes involving lightweight vehicles (K-car) in Japan: A random parameters approach with heterogeneity in means
publications.authors: Wang, L., Lee, J. J., Hu, J., Mao, S., Yang, Y., & Kim, J.
publications.contribution_html: Compares injury-severity factors across single-vehicle and two-vehicle K-car crashes in Japan. Random-parameter probit models with heterogeneity in means and out-of-sample transfer tests examine differences across crash types.
publications.caption: Research schematic prepared from the published abstract; not an original figure.

publications.title: Contributing factors to the severity of crash injury and vehicle damage involving Japanese lightweight vehicles (K-car): Considering unobserved heterogeneity
publications.authors: Wang, L., Lee, J. J., Hu, J., & Mao, S.
publications.contribution_html: Jointly models crash injury and vehicle-damage severity in Japanese lightweight vehicles using random-parameter bivariate probit models with heterogeneity in means. Temporal-stability and out-of-sample analyses examine outcome correlations and unobserved heterogeneity.
publications.image_alt: Injury and vehicle damage — abstract-based schematic
publications.caption: Research schematic prepared from the published abstract; not an original figure.

publications.title: Car following dynamics in mixed traffic flow of autonomous and human-driven vehicles: Complex networks approach
publications.authors: Hu, J., & Lee, J. J.
publications.journal: Physica A: Statistical Mechanics and its Applications
publications.contribution_html: Represents car-following interactions as directed, weighted networks derived from coarse-grained phase-space trajectories. Lyft Level-5 data reveal behavioral differences among autonomous and human-driven vehicle pair types.
publications.caption: Research figure supplied with the original website. Car following dynamics in mixed traffic flow of autonomous and human-driven vehicles: Complex networks approach

publications.title: Vehicle dynamics analytics based on complex network techniques: A trajectory-based visibility graph approach
publications.authors: Hu, J., Gao, D., Wang, L., & Lee, J. J.
publications.contribution_html: Maps vehicle trajectories to visibility graphs with a tunable geometric tolerance. Experiments on highD evaluate lane-keeping and lane-changing recognition, behavioral clustering and associations with surrogate risk indicators.
publications.caption: Research figure supplied with the original website. Vehicle dynamics analytics based on complex network techniques: A trajectory-based visibility graph approach

publications.title: Rethinking driving style recognition: A prediction error-based method
publications.authors: Hu, J., Gao, D., Hu, C., Lee, J. J., Zhou, H., & Abdel-Aty, M.
publications.contribution_html: Infers driving styles by clustering trajectory-prediction errors from a model with attention and convolutional social pooling. Independent kinematic and safety measures provide post-hoc validation across NGSIM traffic-density settings.
publications.caption: Research figure supplied with the original website. Rethinking driving style recognition: A prediction error-based method

publications.title: Re-examining the explanatory boundaries of car-following models through fitting errors decomposition to uncover adaptive feedback
publications.authors: Hu, J., Wang, L., & Lee, J. J.
publications.contribution_html: Decomposes car-following residuals into structural and random components using an unobserved-components model. Across four datasets, the analysis characterizes state dependence and directional relationships; error compensation improves model fitting.
publications.caption: Research figure supplied with the original website. Re-examining the explanatory boundaries of car-following models through fitting errors decomposition to uncover adaptive feedback

publications.title: Meta-learning guided by physics-based residual priors: a plug-and-play training strategy for lightweight car-following models
publications.authors: Hu, J., Bai, J., & Lee, J. J.
publications.journal: Transportation Research Part C: Emerging Technologies
publications.contribution_html: RAMR uses physics-based residual priors and a meta-learning weighting network in bilevel optimization. Tests across four datasets, three physical models and three data-driven predictors assess generalization and computational cost.
publications.caption: Research figure supplied with the original website. Meta-learning guided by physics-based residual priors: a plug-and-play training strategy for lightweight car-following models

publications.title: The robustness benefit of disorder: A global typological analysis of road network morphology and urban performance
publications.authors: Wang, L., Lee, J. J., & Hu, J.*
publications.contribution_html: Examines road-network morphology and urban performance across 70 cities using typological clustering, nonlinear models, dependence analysis and targeted-attack simulations. Results emphasize that robustness relationships depend on city typology.
publications.caption: Research figure supplied with the original website. The robustness benefit of disorder: A global typological analysis of road network morphology and urban performance

publications.title: Dynamic partitioning of heterogeneously loaded road networks: A two-level regionalization scheme with Monte Carlo tree search
publications.authors: Hu, C., Tang, J., Hu, J., Wang, Y., Li, Z., Zeng, J., & Han, C.
publications.journal: Transportation Research Part C: Emerging Technologies
publications.contribution_html: Combines an initial two-level subregion–region partition with Monte Carlo tree search for dynamic boundary adjustment. Experiments on Changsha Yuelu, a grid network and Bilbao assess partitioning under evolving traffic heterogeneity.
publications.caption: Figure 2. Methodological framework. Extracted unchanged from the author-hosted paper.
Research schematic prepared from the published abstract; not an original figure.
publications.title: Public electric vehicle charging under price changes and ambient temperature: Behavioral heterogeneity and managed-charging trade-offs
publications.authors: Qiao, X., Gao, D., Hu, J., & Yang, Y.
publications.contribution_html: Studies behavioral heterogeneity in 441,077 public charging sessions and evaluates managed-charging decisions in a 184-day retrospective replay. The analysis distinguishes price and temperature evidence from predictive screening and quantifies trade-offs among peak relief, recovery delay and destination loading.

publications.caption: Research schematic prepared from the published abstract; not an original figure.
publications.title: BRACE: Boundary-guided, rule-constrained counterfactual augmentation for crash-severity prediction
publications.authors: Hu, J., & Gao, D.
publications.contribution_html: BRACE generates sparse, coding-consistent counterfactual crash records and discounts their weight during retraining. Evaluation on five California counties supports improved F1 most clearly against SMOTEN and TVAE; model-response analyses describe predictive associations rather than causal effects.

publications.title: BRACE: Boundary-guided, rule-constrained counterfactual augmentation for crash-severity prediction
publications.authors: Hu, J., & Gao, D.
publications.contribution_html: BRACE 生成稀疏且符合编码规则的反事实事故记录，并在再训练中降低合成记录权重。五个加州县的数据评估显示，相对 SMOTEN 与 TVAE 的 F1 改善证据最明确；模型响应分析用于解释预测关联，不作因果效应解释。
